learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the chemical building blocks of life! Learn how simple molecules link together to form the complex macromolecules that make up living organisms.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: All the carbon compounds that we get from living tissues are called biomolecules. They are divided into micromolecules (amino acids, sugars) and macromolecules (proteins, DNA, starch).

Polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. They have 4 levels of structure: Primary (sequence), Secondary (helices/sheets), Tertiary (3D folding), and Quaternary (multiple subunits). They act as enzymes, structural components, and antibodies.
Polymers of monosaccharides (simple sugars like glucose) linked by glycosidic bonds. Used for energy storage (starch in plants, glycogen in animals) and structure (cellulose in plant cell walls).
Polymers of nucleotides linked by phosphodiester bonds. A nucleotide has 3 parts: a sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base (A, T, G, C, U). They store and transmit genetic information.
Not true polymeric macromolecules, but they are large water-insoluble molecules. They include fats, oils, and phospholipids (which make up cell membranes). They store long-term energy.

fun_activity.title: 🔗 The Polymer Chain
fun_activity.instructions: Think of Lego blocks! One single 2-bump Lego block is a 'Monomer' (like glucose). When you snap 100 of them together into a long stick, you made a 'Polymer' (like starch). What 'bond' snaps them together?

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember the specific bonds: Amino acids = Peptide bond. Sugars = Glycosidic bond. Nucleotides = Phosphodiester bond.
📌 Lipids are strictly micromolecules based on molecular weight, but they end up in the macromolecular fraction during chemical analysis because they form vesicles.
📌 Proteins are heteropolymers (made of 20 different amino acids), whereas cellulose is a homopolymer (made only of glucose).
quick_recap: ⭐ Primary metabolites have identifiable functions in basic life processes (amino acids, sugars).
⭐ Secondary metabolites (rubber, drugs, spices) are mostly found in plants and fungi and are used for defense or ecological functions.
⭐ The tertiary structure of a protein is absolutely necessary for its biological activity (like acting as an enzyme).
